title: Startup Measurement Rc
objective: Diagnose and harden SEA startup performance by separating launch, bootstrap, evaluation, and cache overhead without weakening strict budgets

oracles: Repeated uncontended component measurements on current SEA artifacts and source runtime

handoff.summary: Added a cross-platform fresh-process startup component reporter for release SEAs. It independently measures bare Node launch, SEA entry/deserialization, empty compiler/REPL setup, first parse/runtime/evaluation, embedded capability-receipt verification, and cold versus warm mpmath import under isolated caches. Every mode-bearing probe now passes explicit --sage or --python arguments, independently of the executable basename. Release measurements enable a shared strict V8 cache observer used by the compiler, Sage/Python runtime bootstrap, and lazy modules; any real cachedDataRejected result names its component and fails the measurement instead of silently recompiling. Ordinary production execution retains V8's safe source-compilation fallback. Controlled comparison on Linux x64 found that current SEA entry and empty startup remain healthy, while first-code startup regressed from about 226 ms at historical commit 802d2ca to 344 ms in Python mode and 385 ms in Sage mode. The generated compiler grew from 5.86 MB to 10.91 MB and the runtime bootstrap from 4.45 MB to 9.41 MB; CPU profiles attribute the cost to executing those eager generated programs, not Tree-sitter or SEA code-cache rejection.
risks: The strict 300 ms full-startup gate is still genuinely red on current Linux x64 artifacts; this lane deliberately does not conceal the regression by changing its budget.

Current self-hosting compiles every src/baselib module, including matrices, polynomials, elliptic curves, and graphics, into both the isolated compiler prologue and user runtime. Splitting a minimal compiler prologue is a compiler-runtime architecture change requiring broad differential validation.

One retained portable failure receipt records missing generated cache files after an intentionally interrupted redundant native build; a clean rebuild followed by the fresh passing portable receipt proves the current workspace. The complete 351-test unit and 433-test integration tiers also pass.
next_steps: Create a compiler-runtime lane that generates and validates a core-only self-hosted compiler prologue separately from the full Sage runtime, then require the current reporter to bring both Sage and Python full startup back below 300 ms.
Run the component report on unsigned macOS arm64 and Windows x64 release artifacts and retain its JSON beside the release-candidate evidence.
Later make non-core Sage facade domains lazy so release startup does not eagerly execute unrelated mathematical implementations.
